design.description: Architecture and what shape a correct implementation should take

decision.description: Unresolved tradeoffs that would change persistence, deployment, integration, or an irreversible route

minimal-change.description: Whether the smallest correct change is enough, and whether extra complexity can be deleted

documents.description: Review of documentation, operator guidance, and other human-facing prose

ui.description: UI, accessibility, responsive layout, and design-system fit

adversarial.description: Work that is irreversible, internally conflicting, or likely to fail when executed, and needs a review that tries to break it

forager-smart.description: Use up front when the mechanism is unsettled: few leads, conflicting evidence, or behavior that must be discovered before a change can be named. Also use after a prior forager attempt hits a substantive dead end and needs a different approach. Named changes stay with forager-worker or forager-capable.

forager-capable.description: Use up front only when a named change depends on coupled invariants or subtle state or concurrency. Backend scope, review remediation, planned tasks, and diagnosis of a located bug stay with forager-worker. If worker versus capable is unclear, use forager-worker. An unsettled mechanism or a dead-end prior attempt goes to forager-smart.

forager-documents.description: Use when the main deliverable is documentation, operator guidance, specs, reports, or other substantial prose and text. forager-worker still owns code changes where documentation is incidental.

forager-ui.description: Use when the main change is user-visible interface behavior, layout, styling, accessibility, React or component state, or UX polish. forager-worker still owns backend work and incidental UI text. Do not dispatch for review-only tasks.

adversarial-plan-reviewer.description: Dispatch in addition to plan-reviewer when the plan has irreversible steps, conflicting requirements, dependency races, or a worker is likely to execute the wrong thing; do not replace that pass. Tell it this is an adversarial pass. Look for evidence the handoff cannot be executed as written.

ui-reviewer.description: Use when the primary review risk is user-visible behavior, accessibility, responsive layout, frontend state, visual regression, or design-system fit. code-reviewer still owns general correctness and backend review. After a behavior-changing UI diff, also dispatch adversarial-code-reviewer; do not replace this pass.

documentation-reviewer.description: Use when the diff is mostly prose: setup flow, operator guidance, terminology, or human-facing documentation. code-reviewer still owns diffs whose primary risk is code correctness, even if docs changed too. When operators will treat the docs as a contract, also dispatch adversarial-documentation-reviewer; do not replace this pass.

adversarial-documentation-reviewer.description: Dispatch in addition to documentation-reviewer when operators will treat the docs as the install, deploy, or recovery contract; do not replace that pass. Tell it this is an adversarial pass. Check guidance against evidence.

adversarial-code-reviewer.description: Dispatch in addition to code-reviewer or ui-reviewer when an implementation changes public contracts, persistence, authorization, concurrency, state transitions, destructive behavior, or other failure-sensitive logic; also use when the first review reports unresolved correctness risk. Skip routine, localized behavior changes with focused verification. Tell it this is an adversarial second pass. Probe false assumptions, missing edge cases, invalid state, and contract breaks.

adversarial-simplicity-reviewer.description: Dispatch in addition to simplicity-reviewer when an implementation introduces or expands abstractions, helpers, configuration, flags, adapters, validation layers, fallback paths, or branching; also use when the diff is materially larger than the requested behavior appears to require. Tell it this is an adversarial pass. Look for deletions and consolidation that preserve behavior.

approach-advisor-xhigh-reasoning.description: Use when a concrete decision would change architecture, persistence, deployment, or integration boundaries. approach-advisor still owns local tradeoffs. If no boundary-changing decision is on the table, stay with approach-advisor. When the route is costly to reverse or competing routes remain, also dispatch adversarial-approach-advisor.

adversarial-approach-advisor.description: Dispatch in addition to approach-advisor when the chosen route is costly to reverse, or competing routes remain plausible; do not replace that pass. Tell it this is an adversarial pass. Challenge the architecture, migration, persistence, deployment, or integration route.

ui-design-advisor.description: Use before planning when audience, information hierarchy, surface structure, interaction model, what the screen should emphasize, or design-system direction is still unresolved.

scout-researcher.description: Search agent. Independent search and questions should be decomposed and fanned out across parallel dispatches rather than folded into one call.

forager-worker.description: Default for named features, fixes, refactors, integrations, review remediation, and verification, including backend, API, and multi-file work. Use forager-capable only when that named change depends on coupled invariants or subtle state or concurrency. Use forager-smart when the mechanism is unsettled or a prior attempt dead-ends.

plan-reviewer.description: Plan reviewer. When the plan has irreversible steps, conflicting requirements, or a likely worker misdirect, also dispatch adversarial-plan-reviewer; do not replace this pass.

code-reviewer.description: Code reviewer. Also dispatch adversarial-code-reviewer when an implementation changes public contracts, persistence, authorization, concurrency, state transitions, destructive behavior, or other failure-sensitive logic, or when this review reports unresolved correctness risk. Skip the adversarial pass for routine, localized behavior changes with focused verification.

simplicity-reviewer.description: Simplicity reviewer. Also dispatch adversarial-simplicity-reviewer when an implementation introduces or expands abstractions, helpers, configuration, flags, adapters, validation layers, fallback paths, or branching, or when the diff is materially larger than the requested behavior appears to require.

approach-advisor.description: Approach advisor. When the route is costly to reverse or competing routes remain, also dispatch adversarial-approach-advisor; do not replace this pass.

vulnerability-reviewer.description: Vulnerability reviewer. Default for application-security review focused on evidenced attacker-to-impact paths and root-cause triage.
